The AI-search thesis, thought through. Search is re-mediating through answer engines, and the ranking currency changed underneath everyone: it's no longer brand-weighted PageRank, it's retrievability — can a crawler reach it, can a model lift a clean claim with a source from it, does the content cohere semantically as expert, is it fresh, is there a stable anchor to cite. That reshuffle is brand-blind, which is the entire stealth opportunity: a tiny publisher whose pages are structurally optimal for machine extraction can win citation share against The Guardian on every query the giants aren't optimizing — and answer engines do link, so citation share becomes referral traffic becomes the subscribe funnel.

What we hold that nobody else does — each verified in the tree today, not aspiration: (1) a per-claim provenance store — the retrieval unit answer engines actually want is the claim-plus-citation, which they currently extract lossily from prose; koios has them pre-extracted, addressable, witness-carrying. No incumbent exposes this; we verified that against four of them yesterday. (2) Live x402 selling — two gateways with real 402 challenges, one with real stranger revenue — precisely as Cloudflare (which fronts koios!) rolls out pay-per-crawl. A news site that natively prices crawler access, on the network building crawler payments, with the payment rail already proven: that convergence is ours alone. (4) The SEAVT/typed-claim theory to make claims machine-composable rather than JSON blobs — the theory-pushing edge the content-mill lane is surfacing right now.
